clue.text: National spin – a piece of cake!

blocks.note: a national of Switzerland
to spin or turn over is to roll

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off a piece of national propaganda as a doddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A piece of cake' looks like the idiom for something easy, but here it is literal: a slice of sponge.
explanation.definitionFit: A rolled sponge filled with jam is a literal item of baking, an example of a cake.

clue.text: Off-the-cuff taking of donations – party official gets the bullet?

blocks.note: a whip enforces discipline among a party's MPs
a round is a single bullet or cartridge

explanation.surface: A party enforcer collects cash on the spot, or else gets sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets the bullet' suggests being fired; instead the official is simply followed by a word for a bullet.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal collection of money among colleagues or friends, gathered impromptu for a gift or cause.

clue.text: Show off direction on organ fingering

blocks.note: S for south, a compass direction
vulgar British slang for masturbation

explanation.surface: An organist is being told how to finger the keys and show off.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests music lessons on a church organ; Private Eye means something far ruder.
explanation.definitionFit: To swank is British informal for to swagger or behave ostentatiously.

clue.text: Cameron's dodgy relationship

indicators.note: something dodgy is unreliable or shady, so the letters are not to be trusted in their given order

blocks.note: the former prime minister's name, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A jibe at David Cameron, the former Conservative prime minister, and some shady liaison of his.
explanation.definitionFit: A love affair is a romantic relationship, so the two words are close synonyms.

clue.text: Dated dumb female totty with new top, attaining oblivion

indicators.note: a new top means the first letter is swapped out for a different one

blocks.note: an old-fashioned term for an attractive but brainless woman
L for learner, a novice, as on a new driver's L-plate

explanation.surface: An airhead gets a makeover and drifts into obscurity.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letter of BIMBO is replaced by L, the learner sign, giving LIMBO.
explanation.definitionFit: Limbo is a state of neglect or being forgotten, close in sense to oblivion.

clue.text: Piss-artist pickpockets getting sod all

blocks.note: a dip is slang for a pickpocket
sod all means nothing, which is zero

explanation.surface: A drunk has his pockets picked, and the thieves find nothing on him.
explanation.walkthrough: Piss-artist is British slang for a heavy drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: A dipso, short for dipsomaniac, is a habitual drunkard, the same as a piss-artist.

clue.text: Old South Americans stifle a real laugh working together

indicators.note: to stifle something is to smother it, so one part is held inside another

blocks.note: the Incas were the ancient people of Peru
something very funny is a hoot

explanation.surface: Ancient Andean people suppress their giggles as they collaborate.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in cahoots is an idiom for colluding or conspiring with someone.

clue.text: Nick, like, upset Brown

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word is read from the bottom up

blocks.note: as is a synonym for like
tan is a light brown colour

explanation.surface: Someone arrests, or steals from, a troubled Gordon Brown, the former Labour prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Brown looks like Gordon Brown; it is only a colour. Old Nick is a traditional name for the Devil.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Nick is a nickname for the Devil, whose proper name in scripture is Satan.

clue.text: A party indiscretion, elevating "pretty boy"

indicators.note: elevating lifts a word upwards, which in a down clue reads it from bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
a do is a party
a sin is a moral lapse

explanation.surface: A slip at a party raises some handsome young man's profile.
explanation.definitionFit: Adonis, the beautiful youth of Greek myth, is used of any very handsome young man.

clue.text: "Miliband ultimately exists": member, to allay doubt and suspicion

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: the last letter of the Labour leader's surname
is means exists
an arm is a limb or member of the body

explanation.surface: A slogan reassures voters that Ed Miliband, the Labour leader, is still around.
explanation.definitionFit: To disarm someone is to win over their hostility or suspicion, removing their defences.

clue.text: Dice cast when pressed by sexual partner to give someone a dose

indicators.note: dice that are cast fall in a random order, so the letters are scrambled
being pressed by something means being squeezed between it, so one part sits inside the other

blocks.note: a mate is a sexual partner
the letters of this word are the fodder

explanation.surface: A gambler under pressure from a lover rolls the dice to dose someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To medicate is to administer a drug, which is to give a dose.

clue.text: (& 30ac./29ac.) As a number of coed pupils, say, might undergo analysis just like Keith Richards?

annotation.answer: BROKEN DOWN BY AGE AND SEX

definitions.text: As a number of coed pupils, say, might undergo analysis just like Keith Richards?

blocks.clueFragment: As a number of coed pupils, say, might undergo analysis
blocks.note: surface reading: statistics on a mixed school's pupils split into categories
setter's reading: the Rolling Stones guitarist, worn out by years and a famously debauched lifestyle

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is a standard way statisticians tabulate a population; applied to Keith Richards, guitarist of the Rolling Stones, it becomes a wrecked old rocker.
explanation.definitionFit: Data analysed by category is split up that way, and a person ruined by years and excess is wrecked the same way.

clue.text: (& 23ac.) Duke and Labour politician getting end away – foul!

indicators.note: getting the end away means the final letter is sent off and dropped

blocks.note: dukes is slang for fists, and a fist is a hand
Ed Balls, the Labour shadow chancellor

explanation.surface: A nobleman and a Labour MP enjoying a sexual encounter is denounced as foul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting one's end away' is British slang for having sex; here it trims a letter. Handball is a football foul for touching the ball with the hand.
explanation.definitionFit: In football, deliberately touching the ball with the arm or hand is an offence, a type of foul.

clue.text: Hawk-like Donald Duck's head after drink and self mutilation

indicators.note: mutilation disfigures and mangles, so the letters are mangled into a new order
the head of a word is its first letter, the only one kept

blocks.note: rum is an alcoholic drink
these four letters are the fodder
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: The surface pictures Donald Duck drunk and self-harming.
explanation.walkthrough: Donald Duck is a red herring: the Donald meant is Donald Rumsfeld, the hawkish US Defense Secretary behind the Iraq war.
explanation.definitionFit: A hawk in politics favours military force; the Bush-era Defense Secretary was the archetypal hawk named Donald.

clue.text: Good-for-nothing Wally, wasted, in the grip of heroin

indicators.note: wasted means wrecked or drunk, so the letters are knocked out of order
something held in the grip of another is enclosed by it

blocks.note: scag is slang for heroin
these five letters are the fodder

explanation.surface: A useless idiot is out of his head, hooked on heroin.
explanation.walkthrough: Wally is British slang for a fool, which suits the surface but is just letters here.
explanation.definitionFit: A scallywag is a rascal or rogue, someone idle and mischievous: a ne'er-do-well.

clue.text: (& 20dn.) When boxer has to take a bite of another boxer that really is competitive?

definitions.text: When boxer has to take a bite of another boxer that really is competitive?

blocks.clueFragment: When boxer has to take a bite of another boxer
blocks.note: surface reading: one prizefighter biting another, as Mike Tyson bit an opponent's ear
setter's reading: a boxer is also a breed of hound, and the idiom for ruthless rivalry is one such animal devouring its own kind

explanation.walkthrough: Boxer is both a fighter and a dog breed; the idiom for cut-throat competition literally describes one dog eating another.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes ruthless rivalry where everyone attacks everyone else to get ahead.

clue.text: A date gives agreement to be taken the other way in much abused car

indicators.text: to be taken the other way
indicators.note: taking something the other way means running it in the opposite direction

blocks.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for date
to give agreement to something is to OK it

explanation.surface: A date agrees to something kinky, apparently in the back of an old banger.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole string A D OKS is read backwards. The Czech car was the butt of many jokes in 1980s Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Skoda is a car marque long mocked in Britain for poor quality, hence much abused.

clue.text: Arse around taking solvers (Private Eye) back to one's earlier activity

indicators.note: to mess around with something is to jumble it, so the letters move
taking something in means holding it inside

blocks.note: these four letters are the fodder
the solvers are addressed as you
a magazine speaks of itself with the editorial we

explanation.surface: Private Eye and its readers are told to stop arsing about and get back to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arse around' is British slang for fooling about, which hides the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The military command 'as you were' orders troops to return to their previous position or activity.

clue.text: Lecher after head from dirty old seafarer

indicators.note: the head taken from a word is its first letter

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
a rake is a dissolute womaniser

explanation.surface: A dirty old sailor is a lecherous type chasing sexual favours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like oral sex in this surface; it is the first letter. Sir Francis Drake was the Elizabethan seafarer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Francis Drake, the Elizabethan navigator who sailed round the world, is a historical seafarer.

clue.text: see 16dn.
Ageless surgery involves ultimate in willy organ replacement (non-functioning)

indicators.note: surgery cuts and rearranges tissue, so these letters are reworked
to involve something is to include it, holding it inside
the ultimate in a word is its final letter

blocks.note: these seven letters are the fodder
the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Anti-ageing surgery goes wrong and the patient's penis no longer works.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to the willy as the organ; the replacement is actually for an eye.
explanation.definitionFit: An artificial eye made of glass replaces a lost eye but gives no sight.

clue.text: After a short period, division in constituency – embarrassing

blocks.note: taken as written
WK is the short form of week
a ward is an electoral subdivision of a borough

explanation.surface: A split in a local party soon after an election proves embarrassing.
explanation.definitionFit: An awkward situation is uncomfortable or embarrassing to be in.

clue.text: see 13ac.
One to roar up back passage?

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom upward

blocks.note: one is the article a
to yell is to roar

explanation.surface: A smutty question about someone going up the back passage.
explanation.walkthrough: Back passage is a euphemism for the anus, but here it is literal: a narrow lane behind houses.
explanation.definitionFit: An alley is a narrow lane running behind buildings, literally a passage at the back.

clue.text: Fine with Nick's end? Granted broadcast, say what's on your mind

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, which alone is kept
something broadcast is heard over the air, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: fine thread is thin
the last letter of the word
granted means permitted

explanation.surface: Nick Clegg, the Lib Dem leader, gets airtime and speaks his mind.
explanation.definitionFit: To voice one's thoughts as they come is an idiom for speaking spontaneously.

clue.text: Thought by Labour's leader "This is as good as it gets"

definitions.text: This is as good as it gets

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its front

blocks.note: an idea is a thought
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A Labour leader's big thought is presented as the best on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour's leader suggests Ed Miliband; only the first letter is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ideal is perfect, the best possible, so nothing could improve on it.

clue.text: Balls pressed by leg, grotesquely, causing protrusion

indicators.note: something grotesque is distorted, so these letters are twisted out of shape
pressed by means squeezed between, so one part sits inside

blocks.note: these three letters are the fodder
Ed Balls, the Labour shadow chancellor

explanation.surface: Testicles squashed against a thigh create an unsightly bulge.
explanation.walkthrough: Balls looks anatomical but is Ed Balls, the Labour politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A ledge is a shelf jutting out from a wall or cliff, a projecting part.

clue.text: Balls at first down by orifice: this produces a whale of a watery ejaculation

definitions.text: this produces a whale of a watery ejaculation

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter, the only one used

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
feeling down is feeling low
a hole is an opening or orifice

explanation.surface: A smutty description of bodily parts producing a spurt of fluid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A whale of' means a great deal of, but it also names the animal whose spout this is.
explanation.definitionFit: A whale's nostril on top of its head spouts a jet of spray when it exhales.

clue.text: see 12ac.
see 12ac.
Black hole generated in tights? Quite singular tights!

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
tights with a run in them are laddered

explanation.surface: A run appears in a pair of black tights, and they are remarkable tights indeed.
explanation.walkthrough: Tight is slang for drunk; 'quite singular tights' plays on the singular, one very tight person. Bladdered is British slang for very drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Bladdered is British slang for extremely drunk, and tight is a milder word for being drunk.
